claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance or an AWS RDS instance.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (as exposed in Pulumi resource properties).
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (as exposed in Pulumi resource properties).
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while not protected by the provider.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' that explains how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance (`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance (`aws.rds.Instance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a resource's own provider-level deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page 'Destroy failures' (/docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/) has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails on a protected resource, the error message names the resource URN and mentions `protect`.
A page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ explaining how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi, e.g. AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
When a cloud-API-enforced protection blocks deletion, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.

For provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, setting the attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough; you must set it to `false`, run `pulumi up`, then run `pulumi destroy`.
Running `pulumi up` after setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` propagates the change to both the live resource and Pulumi's state.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g. in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.

In Azure, `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants (e.g. `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`) create management locks; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
